prompt:
Create an edited pixel-art animation study of this existing Midlife Survivors hero. PRIMARY reference image is enlarged frame 1 of their current walk sheet. SECOND reference is previous idle study, for action staging only. It is too squat and wide: fix proportions to PRIMARY.
Output exactly 8 equal panels, 4 columns x 2 rows, reading left to right then second row. Each panel represents a 56x60 native pixel cell enlarged exactly 8 times: full canvas 1792x960 (448x480 panels). No gutters, captions, shadows or guides. Flat exact magenta #FF00FF background.
Use the primary hero's EXACT proportions, face, costume, material colors and tiny pixel style. This is a SMALL world sprite, NOT a big head portrait/chibi reinterpretation. In each panel figure target native bounds x8 through43 y4 through56 (36 wide 53 high); feet planted at y56, head fixed, center and width fixed. Standing feet side by side, not the walk stride. Preserve primary's head-to-body ratio and narrowness. No zooming, floating, resizing or sliding between frames.
Action glasses push: frames 1-2 relaxed breathing, frame 3 blink, frame 4 rest, frame 5 anticipate, frame 6 free hand rises toward temple, frame 7 index finger pushes glasses up at temple, frame 8 hand returns. Keep mug in the OTHER hand throughout.
Crisp square 8x8 source pixel blocks, no antialiasing. Match primary palette: paper cream, mug orange, navy outlines, khaki slacks or shorts, lavender hoodie for student, navy blazer and tan cowboy hat for cowboy. Neutral white balance, no sepia, golden haze, film tint or palette drift. Every frame identical colors and consistent character identity. Frame 8 smoothly loops to 1.
output_hint:
Generated images are saved to /workspace/generated_images as /workspace/generated_images/exec-9525542a-938e-4484-b51c-c97c71a0b585.png by default.
If you need to use a generated image at another path, copy it and leave the original in place unless the user explicitly asks you to delete it.
The generated image is already displayed to the user. There is no need to render it in the final response as a Markdown image or file link.
